subject.title: [Feature]: Add provider-profile routing policies for multi-account OAuth/API pools (starting with google-gemini-cli)

question: Should OpenClaw add an opt-in provider-profile pool routing contract for batch/worker workloads, and what minimal public config/state surface should ship first?
rationale: The remaining work changes public config, persisted auth state, provider fallback semantics, status/probe output, and upgrade behavior, so automation should not invent those product boundaries or defaults.

options.title: Design Minimal Additive Pool Routing
options.body: Define one opt-in core provider/auth pool contract that keeps existing session-sticky defaults and starts with one observable strategy before adding quota, bucket, and weighting semantics.

options.title: Phase Narrow Requirements Under This Tracker
options.body: Keep this issue canonical while using the related open issues for narrower acceptance criteria around key buckets, same-provider rotation depth, model-specific auth defaults, and pace governance.

options.title: Defer To Sidecar Or Plugin Seam
options.body: Keep current core behavior and recommend external sidecars or future plugin/provider hooks until maintainers decide the native config and state surface is worth the complexity.

recommendation.title: Design Minimal Additive Pool Routing
recommendation.body: Define one opt-in core provider/auth pool contract that keeps existing session-sticky defaults and starts with one observable strategy before adding quota, bucket, and weighting semantics.

likelyOwner.reason: The blocking choice is product/config direction across auth and provider routing, and steipete has the strongest recent history on those boundaries among the identified owners.
